findings.evidence: Adjoin.lean:37-54; Mathlib/RingTheory/Artinian/Algebra.lean:23-37 (`variable [CommRing R] [IsArtinianRing R] [Ring A] [Algebra R A]`; it internally builds `Module.Finite R B` and `IsArtinianRing B` from `hi` alone); Mathlib/RingTheory/IntegralClosure/IsIntegralClosure/Basic.lean:55.
findings.fix: State `theorem coe_inv_mem_adjoin [CommRing K] [IsArtinianRing K] [Ring A] [Algebra K A] {u : Aˣ} (hu : IsIntegral K (u : A)) : ((u⁻¹ : Aˣ) : A) ∈ Algebra.adjoin K {(u : A)}` (the body goes through verbatim, replacing `IsIntegral.of_finite` by `hu` via `isIntegral_algHom_iff`), and pass `IsIntegral.of_finite K (g : Module.End K V)` at the single call site in `IsSemisimple.inv` (Multiplicative.lean:108). `DivisionRing.instIsArtinianRing` (Mathlib/RingTheory/Artinian/Module.lean:376) keeps the field case instance-resolvable.
findings.issue: `Units.coe_inv_mem_adjoin` assumes `[Field K] [FiniteDimensional K A]`, but the only use of finite-dimensionality is deriving `IsIntegral K (u : A)` (lines 46-48); the Mathlib lemma it calls, `IsArtinianRing.isUnit_of_isIntegral_of_nonZeroDivisor`, needs only `[CommRing R] [IsArtinianRing R] [Ring A] [Algebra R A]` plus integrality of the element. A global finiteness assumption on `A` is stronger than the Mathlib convention for this family (`IsIntegral.inv_mem_adjoin`, `IsIntegral.inv_mem`, `IsIntegral.inv` all take an `IsIntegral` hypothesis).

findings.evidence: SemisimplePoint.lean:144-148 vs Multiplicative.lean:127-131 (identical tactic script); Adjoin.lean:94-97 provides only the ℕ transport; `Comodule.pointsAction` is a `MonoidHom` (PointsAction.lean:44), so `map_zpow` applies.
findings.fix: Add `GeneralLinearGroup.ofLinearEquiv_zpow` next to `ofLinearEquiv_pow` (`map_zpow (LinearMap.GeneralLinearGroup.generalLinearEquiv K V).symm e n`), then prove the point-level lemma as `intro M; rw [map_zpow, GeneralLinearGroup.ofLinearEquiv_zpow]; exact (hg M).zpow n`, mirroring the existing `.pow` proof.
findings.issue: `IsSemisimplePoint.zpow` re-runs the `ofNat`/`negSucc` case split verbatim from `GeneralLinearGroup.IsSemisimple.zpow` (Multiplicative.lean:127-131) instead of transporting the general result, because the PR added `ofLinearEquiv_pow` but no `zpow` counterpart.

summary: The GL- and point-level semisimplicity APIs sit at the right level, but the new adjoin lemma carries a global finite-dimensionality hypothesis where only integrality of the single element is used, and the point-level `zpow` re-derives a case split the PR already proves generally.
